default.rationale: Unadmitted TLS registry values remain rejected until their owning decision gate explicitly admits them.

decision.rationale: TLS and DTLS alerts require a typed exhaustive domain before any protocol state machine is admitted.
The bounded record layer preserves every ContentType byte, classifies assigned and unknown values without coercion, and applies exact profile admission.
Handshake message types require generated bounded codecs and state-machine ownership before admission.
Cipher suites, groups, signatures, hashes, and KDF identifiers remain planned until the version-one algorithm decision gate.
PSK exchange modes are deferred to the binder, ticket, resumption, and external-PSK milestones.
Exporter labels remain opaque inputs to a future domain-separated exporter API and are not interpreted at this milestone.
Obsolete certificate, curve, signature, and hash registries feed the complete independently packaged legacy protocol implementations admitted before 1.0.
Supplemental Data, User Mapping, and Authorization Data receive complete separately selected implementations before facade freeze.
Heartbeat message types and modes receive the complete bounded opt-in TLS and DTLS implementation owned by v0.196.1.
SSLKEYLOGFILE labels are forbidden from production crates and reserved for a separately compiled test-support boundary.
Registered RRC message values are owned by the DTLS return-routability engine and cannot be routed through the stream-TLS facade.

default.rationale: Registered extension values require an explicit context and composition decision before version-one completion.

decision.rationale: Brynja transports ALPN protocol identifiers opaquely while the application owns protocol selection and semantics.
Certificate type and status registries are deferred to X.509, raw-public-key, and status-feature milestones.
Every authenticated Cached Information type receives complete bounded implementation and remains explicitly selected.
Certificate compression requires caller-owned bounded providers and explicit negotiation before admission.

default.rationale: ECH configuration extensions remain bounded future work behind the complete ECH configuration and retry policy.
HPKE KEM, KDF, and AEAD identifiers remain future work behind the bounded base-mode implementation.
The QUIC transport owns frames, parameters, errors, and version negotiation outside Brynja's TLS cryptographic adapter.

decision.rationale: Each admitted QUIC version requires an exact version-specific initial-secret and header-protection profile.

default.rationale: Certificate Transparency algorithms, artifacts, logs, and errors remain versioned future validation work.
Unselected SMI namespaces are preserved as caller-owned identifiers and do not gain implicit PKIX semantics.

decision.rationale: PKIX extensions, purposes, algorithms, names, access descriptors, and OCSP identifiers require explicit DER and path-validation handling.

default.rationale: DNS resolution, record processing, and DNSSEC remain caller-owned inputs to ECH configuration selection.

decision.rationale: Current TLS 1.3 remains the primary future stream protocol and is not implemented by this release.
TLS 1.2 is retained only as a separately hardened compatibility engine with no downgrade path.
DTLS 1.3 remains future work in its independent datagram state-machine boundary.
DTLS 1.2 remains a hardened compatibility profile isolated from the DTLS 1.3 engine.
QUIC v1 and v2 cryptography require distinct exact salts, labels, header protection, and version binding.
Canonical identifier, definite minimal length, borrowed value, and bounded constructed traversal form a reusable DER substrate without claiming ASN.1 or X.509 semantics.
Canonical bounded ASN.1 primitive values, calendar times, SET components, and SET OF ordering extend the DER substrate without claiming schema, AlgorithmIdentifier, or X.509 semantics.
Signed X.509 certificates require bounded DER, algorithm consistency, path processing, and identity validation.
The authenticated unsigned X.509 profile receives a complete explicitly non-authenticating typed implementation.
PKCS8, SEC1, and PKCS1 private-key containers require bounded DER and strict algorithm binding.
PEM and certificate-chain containers require bounded decoding and exact label handling.
OCSP parsing, validation, freshness, nonce, transport, and cache semantics remain staged future work.
Certificate Transparency validation remains explicitly versioned future work.
HPKE KEM and context derivation remain bounded cryptographic foundations downstream of validated provider ports.
HPKE Base is implemented first and the remaining RFC 9180 modes receive their own following milestones.
HPKE PSK, Auth, and AuthPSK modes are implemented separately at v0.187.2 through v0.187.4 and closed by v0.187.5.
HPKE export and context lifecycle require bounded output, role separation, exhaustion closure, cancellation, and immediate secret destruction.
ECH remains future work with caller-owned DNS, retry, configuration generation, and inner-name policy.
ECH configuration bootstrap and cache lifecycle require bounded hostile parsing, typed provenance, mandatory-extension handling, expiry, and rotation.
ECH client construction requires exact inner and outer messages, AAD, padding, transcript preservation, GREASE, and resource policy.
ECH server opening requires configuration lookup, uniform HPKE rejection, consistency checks, acceptance confirmation, and bound identity selection.
ECH retry and rotation require exact HelloRetryRequest transcript invariants, retry authority, generation changes, and downgrade detection.
Heartbeat receives a complete bounded opt-in TLS and DTLS implementation and remains disabled by default.
status_request_v2 receives a complete separately selected implementation without changing hardened defaults.
Production SSLKEYLOGFILE export is forbidden because it defeats the secret-lifetime contract.
Key logging may exist only in separately compiled repository test support that cannot enter production packages.
TLS 1.3 post-handshake authentication receives a complete explicit client and server state machine.
Certificate authentication combined with an external PSK receives a complete explicitly selected RFC 9973 profile.
Legacy PKCS1 client CertificateVerify code points receive their complete exact-role compatibility profile.
RFC 9935 ML-KEM PKIX credentials receive complete typed generation, parsing and validation profiles.
Record Size Limit requires directional negotiation, fragmentation and buffering limits, peer-violation handling, and interoperability evidence.
Certificate decompression remains hostile pre-authentication work behind a caller-owned bounded receive provider.
Precompressed certificate artifacts require bounded decompression, canonical byte comparison, complete input binding, and rotation invalidation.
Certificate compression sending requires peer negotiation, current validated artifacts, exact transcript bytes, and fail-closed fallback policy.
The authenticated legacy RFC 6066 facilities receive complete explicit configuration and protocol implementations.
Unknown ignorable extension values are preserved only where the governing protocol explicitly permits safe ignore.
Raw public keys remain an opt-in authentication profile separate from X.509 trust processing.
Delegated credentials require strict lifetime, algorithm, transcript, and certificate binding.

Complete portable byte/bit SHA-1 exists only in the explicit collision-broken legacy leaf with sealed hardened ownership; no modern facade, generic-hash, TLS, PKIX or FIPS edge is admitted. Final consumer and acceleration acceptance remain later milestones.

Complete portable byte/bit MD5 exists only in the explicit collision-broken legacy leaf with sealed hardened ownership; no modern facade, generic-hash, TLS, PKIX or FIPS edge is admitted. Final consumer and acceleration acceptance remain later milestones.

All six FIPS 180-4 SHA-2 identities are fully implemented across ordinary byte, canonical arbitrary-bit, and hardened public/secret profiles with authoritative vectors, compiler-resistant cleanup, separately packaged downstream acceptance, and five explicitly unadmitted CPU candidates.

The private Keccak-f[1600] owner and all six FIPS 202 SHA-3/SHAKE identities are fully implemented across ordinary byte, canonical arbitrary-bit, hardened public/secret, fixed-output and incremental-XOF profiles with two explicitly unadmitted CPU candidates.

The complete SP 800-185 cSHAKE, KMAC/KMACXOF, TupleHash/TupleHashXOF, and ParallelHash/ParallelHashXOF family is planned before 1.0 with exact bit-string encoding, keyed cleanup, portable usability, parallel execution, and cross-backend acceptance.

All four SP 800-185 KMAC and KMACXOF identities are implemented over the hardened cSHAKE owner with complete bit domains, strength-separated constructors, typed secret output, constant-time verification, and non-approved service status.

All four SP 800-185 TupleHash and TupleHashXOF identities are implemented over the hardened cSHAKE owner with structural ordered tuple items, complete arbitrary-bit and exact-length streaming input, fixed and incremental XOF output, typed secret output, and fail-closed incomplete-item handling.

All four SP 800-185 ParallelHash and ParallelHashXOF identities are implemented over the hardened cSHAKE owner with complete arbitrary-bit domains, deterministic allocation-free sequential execution, explicit caller-scheduled leaf ownership, ordered collection, and an isolated bounded std executor.
HMAC-SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA-384 remain future first-party constant-time constructions.
HKDF remains future first-party extract and expand logic with bounded labels and outputs.
AES-128 and AES-256 remain future first-party implementations with architecture-specific review gates.
GHASH finite-field arithmetic remains separate constant-time work with bounded incremental processing and full-width proof obligations.
GHASH and AES-GCM remain future bounded AEAD work with nonce and counter exhaustion enforcement.
ChaCha20 remains separate first-party work with checked block counters and deterministic exhaustion closure.
ChaCha20, Poly1305, and their AEAD composition remain staged first-party future work.
RSA-PSS verification and bounded RSA arithmetic remain future work before any private operation.
P-256, P-384, X25519, ECDSA, and ECDH depend on reviewed fixed-limb field and group operations.
Ed25519 remains future strict verification and signing work with canonical encoding checks.
ML-KEM remains future first-party key-establishment work subject to FIPS 203 and transition policy.

Affine raw-entropy inputs and non-cloneable initialized secure-random state now enforce exact purpose, strength, output, reseed, fork, failure, and destruction duties without treating arbitrary caller bytes as validated entropy.
FIPS entropy-source admission requires exact construction, operational environment, assessment, health tests, and catastrophic failure handling.
The selected SP 800-90A DRBG requires complete instantiate, generate, reseed, uninstantiate, state-protection, and catastrophic-error behavior.
The selected SP 800-90C RBG construction requires exact source and DRBG topology, reseed chains, health propagation, and service boundaries.
Final RFC 10024 and final IANA assignments define exactly three ECDHE-ML-KEM groups for planned v0.164.0 implementation; provisional drafts and private values remain forbidden.
